newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister urges Eurotunnel plan.
newsitem.headline: French minister urges Eurotunnel plan.

text.p: French Transport Minister Jean-Claude Gayssot said on Tuesday it "was in everyone's interests" that Eurotunnel SA/Plc's shareholders approve a plan to restructure its 70 billion francs ($11.8 billion) of bank debt.
Gayssot, who is due to meet Eurotunnel executive chairman Patrick Ponsolle on Wednesday, said that he thought the debt refinancing would be approved at a shareholders' meeting on Thursday.
Gayssot was on a tour of the Channel ports at Boulogne, Calais and Dunkirk.

The French and British governments last week agreed to extend Eurotunnel's licence by 34 years to at least 99 years, provided the debt plan is accepted, rail freight traffic increased through the Channel Tunnel, and in return for 25 percent of its net profits from 2052.
Ponsolle has said he is confident shareholders will back the plan if the company can get a quorum of 25 percent of the shares represented at Thursday's meeting.
If there is no quorum, the company has between five days and two months to call another meeting, with the same quorum requirement.

The debt plan involves 174 lenders taking shares in exchange for eight billion francs of junior-ranked bank loans, which will initially lead to a dilution of current shareholders to 54.5 percent of the common stock.
But with the licence extension, shareholders will get free share warrants exerciseable to 2001, which will limit their dilution by the banks. ($ = 5.907 French Francs)
